scope: Read-only source and official upstream investigation; no builds, implementation changes, acceptance changes, or task-state changes performed by this researcher.
disposition: No supported configuration-only solution found for safe local workspace Rust artifact reuse across physical checkouts with separate Cargo targets. Preserve acceptance; record blocked pending a supported semantics-preserving solution.

sources.reviewed: Official release page identifies v0.19.0 as latest, released 2026-10-24; Rust improvements include locally generated dep-info, not cross-checkout Rust key normalization.

findings: Full compiler arguments are hashed; comment acknowledges full paths and missing normalization (1789-1791).
CARGO_* environment values are hashed with specific unrelated exclusions (1833-1877).
Physical compile cwd is hashed because it appears in the rlib (1878-1879).
Rust backend does not consume SCCACHE_BASEDIRS. Output-directory arguments are excluded, which does not remove source/cwd/environment differences.

sources.reviewed: Proposed Rust SCCACHE_BASEDIRS support normalizes source/remap/environment/cwd key inputs; explicitly warns artifacts using env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) may retain the original checkout path. Not part of pinned official release, and key-only normalization does not establish semantic portability.
Proposed per-request basedirs; currently daemon captures basedirs at startup. Depends on #2813.
Separate macOS proc-macro dylib hashing obstacle: full dylibs contain output paths; proposed metadata-section hashing is not in released support.
Incremental must be disabled; linker-invoking bin/dylib/cdylib/proc-macro crates cannot be cached; env! tracked since Rust 1.46; filesystem-reading proc macros have caveats.

repository_evidence.finding: ToolRoot::local embeds env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) at line21 as its default framework-root authority. Reusing A artifact in B after hashing away the real macro-value difference can silently select A framework pins and sources.

Existing longest-root context mapping supplies portable guest identity and rustc remap flags. Remap flags retain their physical FROM path in actual compiler argv; they do not change physical cwd or Cargo manifest environment values.
Guest preparation adjusts WASI metadata and portable sidecar identity; ordinary host compilation passes through. Sidecar identity is not sccache artifact identity.
Previous wrapper is explicitly composed; child inherits actual cwd, Cargo environment and prepared physical arguments. No existing virtual filesystem or compile-root staging mechanism was found.

rejected_workarounds.reason: Pinned Rust hasher still hashes physical cwd, argument paths and Cargo environment; equivalent outputs alone do not imply equivalent cache keys.

rejected_workarounds.approach: Normalize or discard hashed cwd/CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR only
rejected_workarounds.reason: Can return a cached artifact with A-specific runtime paths in checkout B; concrete tool-root authority example above. Reduces compilation identity rather than proving portability.

rejected_workarounds.approach: Fake common compiler cwd and Cargo manifest environment
rejected_workarounds.reason: Changes compile/runtime path semantics and include/proc-macro behavior; no admitted stable physical namespace exists. Requires a separately designed and validated execution model, not current remap configuration.

rejected_workarounds.approach: Dependency-only hit proof or same-checkout target sharing
rejected_workarounds.reason: Does not satisfy required real local workspace reuse between distinct source paths and empty independent targets.

next_requirement: A supported released implementation and end-to-end portability/admission design must retain actual source/compiler/lock/profile/target identity and runtime tool-root behavior, then pass the task measurement and negative controls. No task acceptance was weakened.
